title: Jesus, in Thee Our Eyes Behold
description: Jesus, in Thee Our Eyes Behold in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 145, headed “Christ and Aaron. Taken from Heb. 7. and 9”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-sus, in thee our eyes be-hold A thou-sand glo-ries more Than the rich gems and pol-ish'd gold The sons of Aa-ron wore.

lines: Jesus, in thee our eyes behold
Than the rich gems and polish'd gold
They first their own burnt-offerings brought
Thy life was pure without a spot,
Fresh blood as constant as the day
But thy one offering takes away
Their priesthood ran thro' several hands.
Once in the circuit of a year
With blood, but not his own,
But Christ by his own powerful blood
And in the presence of our God
Jesus, the King of Glory, reigns
Looks like a lamb that has been slain,
Give him, my soul, thy cause to plead,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
